item.title: Summary for Tropical Storm Pena (CP4/CP042026)
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...PENA MOVING SOUTH OF DUE WEST... As of 11:00 PM HST Tue Nov 10 the center of Pena was located near 10.1, -166.7 with movement W at 9 mph. The minimum central pressure was 1002 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 45 mph.

item.title: Tropical Storm Pena Public Advisory Number 19
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Tue Nov 10 2026 
000
WTPA34 PHFO 110835
TCPCP4
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Pena Advisory Number  19
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP042026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM HST Tue Nov 10 2026
 
...PENA MOVING SOUTH OF DUE WEST...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 PM HST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...10.1N 166.7W
ABOUT 495 MI...795 KM SSE OF JOHNSTON ISLAND
ABOUT 970 MI...1560 KM SW OF HONOLULU HAWAII
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...45 MPH...75 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 260 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1002 MB...29.59 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 PM HST (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Pena was
located near latitude 10.1 North, longitude 166.7 West. Pena is
moving toward the west near 9 mph (15 km/h), and this general
motion is expected for the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 45 mph (75 km/h) with higher gusts.
Little change in strength is forecast during the next day or so,
followed by gradual weakening through Friday.

Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 115 miles (185 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1002 mb (29.59 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 500 AM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Blake

item.title: Tropical Storm Pena Forecast Discussion Number 19
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Tue Nov 10 2026 
571 
WTPA44 PHFO 110836
TCDCP4
 
Tropical Storm Pena Discussion Number  19
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP042026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM HST Tue Nov 10 2026
 
Convection continues to wax and wane near Pena, with most of the
current activity well north of the center.  A WSFM microwave pass
and a SAR pass from a few hours ago showed the system was moving 
south of west, and all of the tropical-storm-force winds were
north of the center.  The current intensity is kept at 40 kt,
consistent with the SAR data and just above a recently received 
ASCAT scatterometer pass.
 
Pena's motion is estimated to be 260/8 kt. The cyclone continues to
be steered by a high pressure ridge centered over the subtropical 
Central Pacific, and the high should cause the storm to accelerate 
westward during the next few days.  The most notable change is that 
the guidance has shifted slightly to the south, probably because 
the storm is still losing latitude.  The new NHC track forecast is 
nudged in that direction, close to a blend of the Google DeepMind 
ensemble and the HFIP Corrected Consensus models.
 
Despite the storm being over very warm waters with decent mid-level
humidity values, there is some westerly shear noted below the
outflow layer because of stronger low-level flow and weak mid- 
to upper-level flow. The environment is not expected to change much 
during the next few days, but a small increase in shear and 
decrease in moisture is noted by Thursday.  This should be enough 
to cause weakening by then, and the system could dissipate in a few 
days while it is near the International Dateline due to a 
persistence of these unfavorable conditions, or an increase in 
forward speed that causes the weak cyclone to open up into a 
trough.  The intensity forecast is reduced slightly from the last 
one, and the dissipation time has been brought forward, similar to 
the latest global model consensus solution.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  11/0900Z 10.1N 166.7W   40 KT  45 MPH
 12H  11/1800Z 10.0N 168.4W   40 KT  45 MPH
 24H  12/0600Z 10.2N 171.2W   40 KT  45 MPH
 36H  12/1800Z 10.6N 174.3W   35 KT  40 MPH
 48H  13/0600Z 11.0N 177.4W   35 KT  40 MPH
 60H  13/1800Z 11.4N 179.5E   30 KT  35 MPH
 72H  14/0600Z...DISSIPATED
 
$$
Forecaster Blake
